### Target buyer persona

**Who buys:** the person who owns the member app or the program inside it. At app-first brands (A, D) that is the founder or CEO, together with the product head. At studio and club networks (B) it is head office: CEO or general manager, digital or product, and programming or training. At fitness software platforms (E, added 2026-11-20) it is the founder or CEO together with the product head; the platform would offer the scan to its own gym, studio and coach customers inside the app it already runs. Partnerships owners are a way in at every group.

- **Founder, CEO, Managing Director, General Manager (A, B, D).** Owns differentiation and the subscription or membership bet. Cares about members who stay past the first month and about paid-tier take-up. Objection: "Will members actually scan?" Answer: the pilot measures scan completion and repeat scans separately, and the product team chooses where the scan sits.
- **Chief Product Officer, Head of Product, Product Manager or Owner, Head of Digital (A, B, D).** Owns build or buy and the check-in flow. Cares about activation, onboarding completion and roadmap load. Objection: "A scan step could hurt onboarding completion." Answer: the page's FAQ says it can; the scan can sit at the first check-in, and the pilot compares onboarding completion with the usual flow.
- **Head of Programming, Training, Education or Fitness; Head Coach; National Fitness Manager (A, B, D).** Owns how coaches and instructors review progress. Cares about program adherence and coach time. The page's coach line is their lane: the coach reviews the same record before setting the next program block.
- **Head of Partnerships, Partnerships Manager, Business Development Manager (all groups).** Owns third-party features in the member offer. The `partnerships` lane, and a route in below C-level (PPL-1, PPL-3).
- **Founder, CEO, CPO, Head of Product, Head of Partnerships or Integrations (E).** Owns what the platform puts in front of its customers' members and which partner features ship in it. Cares about features that help its gym, studio and coach customers keep members, and about the integration load on its own team. Objection: "Our customers would each have to switch it on." Answer: the scan sits inside the app the platform already ships, under the platform's look, and a pilot with one customer's member cohort measures take-up. The `platform` lane.
- **CTO, Head of Technology, Head of Engineering (A, B, E).** Implementer and internal champion, not the economic buyer: `technical-integration`, P3, at most two per company.
- **Franchisees, studio and club owners, franchise business managers (B):** `referral`. They point to head office and are never pitched adoption.

**What they care about (KPIs):** day-30 and day-90 retention; free-to-premium or class-pack to membership conversion; onboarding completion; program adherence.

**Likely objections:** members will not scan (the pilot measures it); onboarding friction (the scan can move to the first check-in); "we already measure members in the club" (the phone scan covers the check-ins between visits, said without naming any device); "we could build it" (a pre-trained model through SDK and API, with no computer-vision team to hire); privacy (replies only, from `compliance.md` §10 with the FAQ link); price (replies only, from the public page).

**Not the buyer:** marketing, brand, social, content and PR; CRM, lifecycle, retention and growth marketing (PPL-3: 0/44); customer service and member support; membership sales and front desk; finance, legal, HR and payroll; non-clinical operations without app ownership, COO included (PPL-3: 0/55); customer success, revenue operations and sales at platforms (E); engineers below head level; individual personal trainers and instructors without a head-office role; investors and board members.

### Anti-cases (where it does NOT work)

- **Competitors and their partners:** any company whose own product is body scanning or body measurement from images or in-club hardware, and companies whose app embeds a competitor's scan. A brand that offers an in-club scanner stays IN, and copy never mentions the scanner.
- **Displacement:** a company that already runs a phone-camera body scan, or has signed a phone-scanning vendor, is HOLD for Vadim.
- **No owned app:** a brand whose only app is a booking app run by a vendor or an overseas franchisor, with no program in it and no head-office control. OUT.
- **Marketplaces and aggregators** (Fitness Passport, Wellhub, ClassPass, TotalPass, Urban Sports Club and similar): OUT in all four sibling campaigns.
- **Health funds and insurers:** out of this campaign (Vadim 2026-11-19).
- **Free consumer apps with no paid tier and no coach,** and product-only nutrition, supplement and apparel brands.
- **Women's health, fertility, pregnancy and postnatal-led apps** (population anti-case), and youth programs.
- **Public entities:** council leisure centres, state sports institutes, public health services.
- **Clinical and MSK providers** (physiotherapy groups, exercise-physiology clinics): the conversation would be clinical.
- **Head office or parent in the US or the UK:** routes to `nick` or `katerina` (Centr; The Fast 800; inLIFE Wellness while its head office is listed in Dallas). F45 is out in every sibling campaign.
- **The October hold:** the 44 companies of `2026-10-11-au-sport-fitness` and the brands they own, until its invites are out and its replies are classified.
- **AIA Australia, Mosh and The Healthy Mummy** (live threads); **Everlab** (declined, until 2027-04-14); customers with a contract.
- **Stop conditions before send:** a target announces a sale, a closure or a body-scanning partner (pause, Vadim decides); a profile shows the person has left (drop, or treat as a referral if they name a successor).

## What past campaigns taught (learnings.md 2026-10-30, verbatim)

Campaign rules above win over these. `[directional]` is the default; say why when you depart from it. `[watch]` is not a rule yet.

### People

**PPL-1 [directional] Seniority runs backwards.** C-level and founders replied to 5/344
invites, everyone below them to 37/1064. The validator's P1 tier: 2/200; P3 and P4 together:
29/671. Keep decision-makers on the list, but do not give P1 for title alone, and give every IN
account at least one route-in below C-level (programme, clinical, practitioner or partnerships
lead) when the export has one. Part of the gap is C-level people not accepting strangers'
invites; the rates are per invite.

**PPL-2 [directional] The referral ask is a way in.** `referral` lane: 21/475 replied; buyer
lanes: 21/958. Referral replied at least as often as buyer lanes in 5 of the 6 campaigns that
had both. A non-buyer at an IN account in a relevant function is a referral-lane PASS, not a FAIL.

**PPL-3 [directional] Functions that do not answer.** Per person contacted: marketing 0/52,
retention / CRM / growth 0/44, non-clinical operations 0/55, engineering 1/90. Partnerships, BD
and sales: 6/83, the highest. Clinical operations titles count as clinical, not operations.
Do not fill an account's cap with marketing, CRM or engineering people.

**PPL-4 [directional] Who the positive repliers were.** Of 34 positive repliers, 3 were C-level.
The rest: coaching lead, Tier 3 practitioner lead, obesity consultant, dietitian, clinical
operations lead, head of commercial, regional partnerships manager, director of clinical
programmes, senior director of clinical research, GM health and wellbeing.

## ICP segment (icp-detail.md, verbatim)

### 8. Connected & Digital Fitness

**What they are:** connected fitness platforms, digital fitness apps, virtual personal training, wellness & coaching apps, fitness subscription platforms, AI-powered fitness tech, corporate wellness & fitness platforms.

**Buyer titles:**
- Founder / CEO
- Chief Product Officer
- Head of Growth
- VP User Engagement / VP Engagement / Retention
- CTO
- Product Manager
- Digital Experience Manager
- Fitness Program Director
- Innovation & Partnerships Team

**Company size & revenue:** Series B-public. **$1M+ annual revenue** — сильный фокус на recurring subscriptions/retention.

**Geo:** US, UK, Canada, Germany, UAE, Australia, Nordics.

**Pain points — Product & Engagement:**
- Пользователи теряют мотивацию без visible progress
- Слабый long-term retention
- Общие рекомендации, ограниченная персонализация
- Low-value методы трекинга

**Pain points — Operational & Business:**
- Сложно дифференцироваться от конкурентов
- Высокий churn после onboarding
- Растущий CAC требует более сильного engagement
- Пользователи ожидают AI-персонализацию

**KPIs:** subscription retention, daily/weekly active users, trainer-to-member ratio efficiency.

**Examples to target (verify status before outreach):** Peloton (digital), Future, Centr, Fitbod, Tonal, Freeletics, Zing Coach, Verv; Corporate Wellness: Wellhub, Virgin Pulse; Whoop (adjacent, для benchmarking).
